title: Merton jump-diffusion European call, Poisson series
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K [M], T [M], r, q, sigma, lambda (per year), mu_J, sigma_J (log-jump mean/sd); n_max terms. DITANYAKAN: Merton call price per contract (currency) and difference to BS(sigma) without jumps. RUMUS: Card 1-2: kbar = e^{mu_J+sigma_J^2/2}-1, L = lambda(1+kbar), r_n = r - lambda kbar + n ln(1+kbar)/T, sigma_n^2 = sigma^2 + n sigma_J^2/T; C = sum_n Pois(n; L T) BS(S,K,r_n,sigma_n,T,q); toolkit bs_price for each term. JAWAB: 1) kbar, L. 2) loop n=0..n_max: weight, r_n, sigma_n, BS term. 3) sum, check tail weight < tol. 4) BS without jumps for comparison. 5) check price >= intrinsic lower bound, decreasing in K.
formulas: w_n = e^{-L T}(L T)^n/n!, L = lambda(1+kbar)
r_n = r - lambda kbar + n ln(1+kbar)/T
pitfalls: sigma_n^2 without /T; r_n must enter both d1 and the strike discount

title: Merton jump-diffusion put and put-call parity check
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K [M], T [M], r, q, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J. DITANYAKAN: Merton put per contract and parity residual C - P - (S e^{-qT} - K e^{-rT}). RUMUS: Card 2 series with BS put terms (bs_price kind='put'); parity holds term by term because each term is a BS price with consistent r_n and the compensator keeps E[S_T] = S e^{(r-q)T}. JAWAB: 1) series call. 2) series put (same weights, r_n, sigma_n). 3) residual per contract. 4) check |residual| at machine precision; nonzero means compensator or r_n missing.
formulas: C - P = S e^{-qT} - K e^{-rT}
pitfalls: parity failure signals missing compensator -lambda kbar

title: Merton price via lambda-weights and shifted spot S_n
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K [M], T, r, q, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J; statement may write weights with lambda T and S_n. DITANYAKAN: Price from the alternative form and agreement with the L-weight / r_n form. RUMUS: Card 2 alternative: C = sum_n Pois(n; lambda T) BS(S_n, K, r, sigma_n, T), S_n = S (1+kbar)^n e^{-lambda kbar T} (adjusted for jump mean e^{n mu_J + n sigma_J^2/2}). Follow the statement literally if it mixes forms. JAWAB: 1) kbar. 2) per n: lambda-weight, S_n, sigma_n, BS with r. 3) sum. 4) compute L-form too; report abs diff (should be ~0). 5) pick the form the text names.
pitfalls: mixing lambda-weights with r_n silently changes the price; follow the text

title: Merton jump-diffusion Monte Carlo price with standard error
deliverables: per-contract table: mc_price, standard_error, closed_form, z_score
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, K [M], T, r, q, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J; N_steps, N_paths, seed. DITANYAKAN: MC price, SE, closed-form series price and z = (mc - cf)/SE. RUMUS: Card 1; toolkit simulate_jump_diffusion(S0,r,q,sigma,lambda_j,mu_j,sigma_j,T,N_steps,N_paths,seed) returns S_T [N_paths]; log step drift (r-q-lambda kbar - sigma^2/2)dt, jump sum N mu_J + sqrt(N) sigma_J Z, N ~ Pois(lambda dt). JAWAB: 1) S_T [N_paths]. 2) payoff per contract [M x N_paths]. 3) price = e^{-rT} mean; SE = e^{-rT} std(ddof=1)/sqrt(N) (antithetic: SE on pair averages). 4) series price. 5) check |z| < 3, mean(S_T) e^{-(r-q)T} ~ S0.
formulas: ln S_{t+dt} = ln S_t + (r-q-lambda kbar - sigma^2/2)dt + sigma sqrt(dt) Z + sum jumps
pitfalls: antithetic pairs are not independent: SE from pair means

title: Merton implied volatility smile across strikes
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, strikes [M], T, r, q, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J. DITANYAKAN: Merton prices and BS implied vols per strike (decimal); smile shape. RUMUS: Card 2 series, then toolkit implied_vol(price,S,K,T,r,kind,q) per strike. JAWAB: 1) price per strike. 2) implied vol by root-finding on BS. 3) BS(iv) reprices check. 4) report iv [M]; skew = slope of iv vs ln(K/F). 5) check negative mu_J gives iv decreasing in K (downward skew), iv >= sigma near ATM.
pitfalls: out-of-range iv bracket for deep OTM; use OTM option side

title: Merton parameter MLE from daily log returns
deliverables: summary json: mu, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J, loglik
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices [T+1] (daily), dt = 1/252; n_max terms; starting values. DITANYAKAN: MLE of mu, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J (annualised), max log-likelihood. RUMUS: Card 3 density: sum_n Pois(n; lambda dt) N(x; (mu - sigma^2/2 - lambda kbar)dt + n mu_J, sigma^2 dt + n sigma_J^2); log-sum-exp over n; L-BFGS-B with bounds sigma, sigma_J > 0, lambda >= 0. JAWAB: 1) x = diff ln S [T]. 2) neg LL function. 3) several deterministic starts; keep best LL. 4) report per-year parameters. 5) check annual variance sigma^2 + lambda(mu_J^2+sigma_J^2) ~ sample var/dt.
formulas: f(x) = sum_n Pois(n; lambda dt) phi(x; m_n, v_n)
m_n = (mu - sigma^2/2 - lambda kbar)dt + n mu_J
pitfalls: unbounded LL when one component collapses (sigma_J -> 0); bound it

title: Merton log-return moments: variance, skewness, excess kurtosis
deliverables: summary json: mean, variance, skewness, excess_kurtosis per horizon
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J; horizon tau (years) [n_h]. DITANYAKAN: Cumulant-based mean, variance, skewness, excess kurtosis of ln(S_tau/S_0). RUMUS: Cumulants: k1 = (mu - sigma^2/2 - lambda kbar)tau + lambda tau mu_J; k2 = sigma^2 tau + lambda tau (mu_J^2+sigma_J^2); k3 = lambda tau (mu_J^3 + 3 mu_J sigma_J^2); k4 = lambda tau (mu_J^4 + 6 mu_J^2 sigma_J^2 + 3 sigma_J^4). skew = k3/k2^1.5, exkurt = k4/k2^2. JAWAB: 1) cumulants per horizon. 2) standardise. 3) check skew sign = sign(mu_J), kurtosis decays as 1/tau.

title: Risk-neutral martingale check of simulated jump-diffusion
deliverables: summary json: mean_discounted_ST, S0, rel_error, se
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, T, r, q, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J; N_paths, seed. DITANYAKAN: E[e^{-(r-q)T} S_T] from MC vs S0, with SE; with and without compensator. RUMUS: Card 1: compensator -lambda kbar in drift makes e^{-(r-q)t} S_t a martingale. toolkit simulate_jump_diffusion. JAWAB: 1) simulate S_T. 2) discounted mean and SE. 3) rerun with compensator removed to show bias S0(e^{lambda kbar T} - 1). 4) report relative error; check within 3 SE.
formulas: bias without compensator: S0 e^{(r-q)T}(e^{lambda kbar T}-1)
pitfalls: missing compensator inflates call prices

title: Merton price via characteristic function and FFT (Carr-Madan)
deliverables: per-strike table: K, fft_price, series_price, abs_diff
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K [M], T, r, q, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J; FFT N, eta, damping alpha. DITANYAKAN: Call prices on the FFT log-strike grid interpolated to K, vs series. RUMUS: phi(u) = exp(i u (ln S + (r-q-sigma^2/2-lambda kbar)T) - sigma^2 u^2 T/2 + lambda T (e^{i u mu_J - sigma_J^2 u^2/2} - 1)); Carr-Madan psi(v) = e^{-rT} phi(v-(alpha+1)i)/(alpha^2+alpha-v^2+i(2alpha+1)v); lambda_k = 2pi/(N eta). JAWAB: 1) build phi. 2) Simpson weights, FFT. 3) C(k) = e^{-alpha k}/pi Re(...). 4) interpolate to ln K. 5) compare with series; check |diff| small and monotone in K.
formulas: phi_X(u) = exp(i u m T - sigma^2 u^2 T/2 + lambda T(phi_J(u)-1))
pitfalls: grid spacing trade-off eta x lambda = 2pi/N; alpha too large overflows

title: Merton calibration to an option price surface
deliverables: summary json: sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J, rmse
frame: DIKETAHUI: market prices or iv [M] with S, K, T, r, q; initial guess, bounds. DITANYAKAN: Calibrated sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J and per-contract fit errors. RUMUS: Card 2 series as model; minimise sum (C_model - C_mkt)^2 (or iv errors / vega-weighted); toolkit bs_price, implied_vol. JAWAB: 1) market prices (from iv if given). 2) objective over [M]. 3) L-BFGS-B multi-start. 4) per-contract errors, RMSE. 5) check parameters inside bounds, mu_J < 0 if skew is downward.
pitfalls: identification: sigma and lambda sigma_J^2 trade off; report starts tried

title: Merton series truncation and convergence
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J; tolerance. DITANYAKAN: Partial sums by n_max and the smallest n_max with tail below tolerance. RUMUS: Card 2; tail bound: remaining Poisson mass 1 - sum_{n<=N} Pois(n; L T) times max term (<= S). JAWAB: 1) partial sums n = 0..N. 2) increments. 3) Poisson tail mass. 4) report minimal n_max. 5) check monotone convergence and price stable at tol.

title: Kou double-exponential jump compensator and moments
deliverables: summary json: kbar, mean_jump, var_jump, annual_variance
frame: DIKETAHUI: p, eta1 > 1, eta2 > 0, lambda, sigma. DITANYAKAN: kbar, log-jump mean and variance, annual variance of log returns. RUMUS: Card 4: kbar = p eta1/(eta1-1) + (1-p) eta2/(eta2+1) - 1; E[Y] = p/eta1 - (1-p)/eta2; E[Y^2] = 2p/eta1^2 + 2(1-p)/eta2^2. JAWAB: 1) check eta1 > 1 (else E[e^Y] infinite). 2) kbar. 3) jump moments. 4) annual variance sigma^2 + lambda E[Y^2]. 5) report.
pitfalls: eta1 <= 1 makes the compensator infinite

title: Kou jump-diffusion option price by Monte Carlo
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, K [M], T, r, q, sigma, lambda, p, eta1, eta2; N_paths, seed. DITANYAKAN: MC price and SE per contract. RUMUS: Card 4; terminal sampling: N ~ Pois(lambda T), each jump Y = Exp(eta1) w.p. p else -Exp(eta2); ln S_T = ln S0 + (r-q-sigma^2/2-lambda kbar)T + sigma sqrt(T) Z + sum Y. JAWAB: 1) kbar. 2) draw N, Z, jumps (vectorised by total count). 3) payoff, discount. 4) SE = std/sqrt(N). 5) check martingale mean of S_T.
pitfalls: numpy exponential takes SCALE = 1/eta

title: Kou characteristic function and Fourier price
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K [M], T, r, q, sigma, lambda, p, eta1, eta2; FFT settings. DITANYAKAN: Fourier call prices per strike. RUMUS: phi_Y(u) = p eta1/(eta1 - i u) + (1-p) eta2/(eta2 + i u); phi_X(u) = exp(i u (ln S + (r-q-sigma^2/2-lambda kbar)T) - sigma^2 u^2 T/2 + lambda T (phi_Y(u) - 1)); Carr-Madan as for Merton. JAWAB: 1) phi. 2) damped FFT. 3) interpolate to K. 4) compare with MC within 3 SE. 5) check monotone in K.
formulas: phi_Y(u) = p eta1/(eta1 - iu) + (1-p) eta2/(eta2 + iu)
pitfalls: damping alpha must satisfy alpha + 1 < eta1

title: Jump detection in returns and jump parameter estimates
deliverables: summary json: n_jumps, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J, sigma_diffusion
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices [T+1] daily (dates sorted), dt = 1/252, threshold c (default 3). DITANYAKAN: Count of jumps, lambda (per year), mu_J and sigma_J of flagged returns, diffusive sigma on non-jumps. RUMUS: Card conventions: flag |r - mean| > c std(r, ddof=1); lambda = n_jumps/(n dt); mu_J, sigma_J = mean/std(ddof=1) of flagged; sigma = std(non-flagged)/sqrt(dt) if stated. JAWAB: 1) log returns [T]. 2) mean, std. 3) flags. 4) lambda, mu_J, sigma_J. 5) optional sigma re-estimate. 6) check lambda >= 0, jump share small.
pitfalls: n = number of returns = len(prices) - 1, not number of prices

title: Comparative statics of Merton price in jump parameters
frame: DIKETAHUI: base S, K, T, r, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J; bump sizes. DITANYAKAN: Price change for bumps in lambda, mu_J, sigma_J, sigma (finite differences). RUMUS: Card 2 series; central difference (P(x+h)-P(x-h))/(2h). JAWAB: 1) base price. 2) bump each parameter up/down. 3) derivatives. 4) check dprice/dsigma_J > 0, dprice/dlambda > 0 for ATM.

title: Merton jump-diffusion terminal VaR and ES of a stock position
frame: DIKETAHUI: position value V0 (or shares x S0), horizon h, mu, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J; level alpha; N, seed. DITANYAKAN: VaR and ES of loss over h (currency), vs normal-sigma VaR. RUMUS: Card 3 simulate log returns over h; loss = V0(1 - e^{R}); VaR_a = sorted[ceil(a n)-1]; ES = mean of losses > VaR. toolkit var_es_normal for comparison. JAWAB: 1) simulate R [N]. 2) losses. 3) sort, VaR, ES. 4) normal VaR with total variance. 5) check ES >= VaR, jump VaR >= normal VaR in tail.
pitfalls: np.quantile linear vs type-1 quantile (V4)

title: Bernoulli vs Poisson jump discretisation in simulation
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, K, T, r, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J; dt grid; N, seed. DITANYAKAN: Prices with N ~ Pois(lambda dt) vs Bernoulli(lambda dt) per step; bias vs dt. RUMUS: Card pitfall: equal only for small lambda dt; Bernoulli truncates multiple jumps per step. JAWAB: 1) same normals for both. 2) per dt: two price estimates. 3) difference and SE. 4) check diff -> 0 as dt -> 0.

title: Return descriptives and normality test motivating jumps
deliverables: summary json: mean, std, skew, excess_kurtosis, jb_stat, jb_pvalue
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices [T+1] (sorted dates). DITANYAKAN: Annualised mean/vol, skew, excess kurtosis (pandas G2), JB stat and p-value. RUMUS: Card V3: skew/kurt bias-corrected as pandas; JB = n/6 (S^2 + K^2/4) with population moments (scipy); vol = std(ddof=1) sqrt(252). JAWAB: 1) log returns [T]. 2) moments. 3) JB, chi2(2) p. 4) report; check excess kurtosis > 0 suggests jumps.
pitfalls: mixing raw Pearson kurtosis with excess (V3)

title: Compound Poisson aggregate loss moments
deliverables: summary json: mean, variance, sd, skewness
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda (claim count mean), severity family and parameters (or E[X], E[X^2], E[X^3]). DITANYAKAN: E[S], Var[S], sd, skewness of S = sum X_i. RUMUS: Card 5: E = lambda E[X], Var = lambda E[X^2], third central = lambda E[X^3]; skew = lambda E[X^3]/(lambda E[X^2])^1.5; toolkit compound_poisson_moments(lam, sev_mean, sev_second_moment, sev_third_moment). JAWAB: 1) severity raw moments (lognormal e^{k mu + k^2 s^2/2}; Pareto finite only for k < a). 2) aggregate moments. 3) check skew > 0.
pitfalls: Var uses E[X^2], not Var[X]

title: Aggregate loss distribution by FFT with lognormal severity, VaR and ES
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda, lognormal (mu, s); span h, n points; level alpha. DITANYAKAN: Aggregate pmf on grid, VaR_alpha and ES (currency). RUMUS: Card 5; toolkit severity_dist('lognormal',...), discretize_severity(dist,h,n,'rounding'), compound_poisson_fft(lam, pmf, n), aggregate_var_es(pmf,h,level), aggregate_moments(pmf,h); suggest_lattice for h, n. JAWAB: 1) choose h, n so n h >> tail (suggest_lattice). 2) rounding pmf f_k. 3) g = Re ifft(exp(lambda(fft(f)-1))) with padding. 4) VaR = smallest x with CDF >= alpha; ES. 5) check sum g = 1, mean ~ lambda E[X].
pitfalls: span too short -> wrap-around aliasing piles tail mass at small x

title: Panjer recursion for compound Poisson
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda, discretised severity pmf f [n] on span h (f_0 may be > 0); n. DITANYAKAN: Aggregate pmf g [n], CDF, quantile. RUMUS: Panjer Poisson: a = 0, b = lambda; g_0 = exp(lambda(f_0 - 1)); g_k = (lambda/k) sum_{j=1..k} j f_j g_{k-j}. toolkit panjer_poisson(lam, severity_pmf, n). JAWAB: 1) severity pmf. 2) g_0. 3) recursion. 4) CDF, moments. 5) check sum ~ 1 and mean ~ lambda E[X].
pitfalls: underflow of g_0 for large lambda: start at a shifted point or use FFT

title: Panjer recursion with negative binomial claim count
frame: DIKETAHUI: negative binomial (r, beta) count; discretised severity f [n]. DITANYAKAN: Aggregate pmf, moments, VaR. RUMUS: (a,b,0): a = beta/(1+beta), b = (r-1) beta/(1+beta); g_0 = (1 + beta(1 - f_0))^{-r}; g_k = 1/(1 - a f_0) sum_j (a + b j/k) f_j g_{k-j}. toolkit panjer_negbin(r, beta, pmf, n) or panjer_ab. JAWAB: 1) a, b, p0-pgf at f_0. 2) recursion. 3) mean check r beta E[X]; Var = r beta E[X^2] + r beta^2 E[X]^2. 4) VaR.
formulas: g_k = sum_j (a + b j/k) f_j g_{k-j} / (1 - a f_0)
pitfalls: NB parametrisation (r, beta) vs (r, p): p = 1/(1+beta)

title: Panjer recursion with binomial claim count
frame: DIKETAHUI: m policies, claim probability q; discretised severity f [n]. DITANYAKAN: Aggregate pmf and moments. RUMUS: Binomial (a,b,0): a = -q/(1-q), b = (m+1) q/(1-q); g_0 = (1 - q + q f_0)^m; toolkit panjer_binomial(m, q, pmf, n). JAWAB: 1) a, b, g_0. 2) recursion. 3) check mean m q E[X], support bounded by m max X.

title: FFT vs Panjer cross-check of the aggregate distribution
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda, severity pmf f [n], h. DITANYAKAN: Max |g_fft - g_panjer|, quantiles from each. RUMUS: toolkit compound_poisson_fft and panjer_poisson on the same lattice; general pgf via compound_fft(severity_pmf, pgf). JAWAB: 1) same f. 2) both pmfs. 3) max diff; if large, pad FFT (2n or more). 4) report VaR from both. 5) check agreement to ~1e-10.
pitfalls: no zero padding -> FFT circular convolution aliasing

title: Severity discretisation: rounding vs local moment matching
frame: DIKETAHUI: severity cdf F (family, params), span h, n. DITANYAKAN: Discretised pmfs and their means vs true E[X]. RUMUS: Rounding: f_0 = F(h/2), f_k = F((k+.5)h) - F((k-.5)h); lower/upper bounds f_k = F(kh) - F((k-1)h) shifted; toolkit discretize_severity(dist, h, n, method, tail). JAWAB: 1) severity_dist. 2) each method. 3) means; rounding approx unbiased, lower/upper bracket. 4) tail handling (drop vs lump at end).
pitfalls: tail mass beyond n h dropped -> pmf sums < 1

title: Aggregate loss Monte Carlo with Pareto severity
deliverables: summary json: mean, var_alpha, es_alpha, se_mean
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda, Pareto (x_m, a); level alpha; n_sims, seed. DITANYAKAN: MC mean, VaR, ES of S. RUMUS: Card completing inputs: numpy pareto is Lomax -> X = (rng.pareto(a)+1) x_m; E = a x_m/(a-1). toolkit compound_poisson_mc(lam, sampler, n_sims, seed). JAWAB: 1) N ~ Pois(lambda) [n_sims]. 2) sum severities. 3) sort; VaR = sorted[ceil(alpha n)-1]; ES mean above. 4) check mean vs lambda E[X] (a > 1).
pitfalls: using rng.pareto without +1 and x_m scaling

title: Compound Poisson with gamma severity parametrisation
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda, gamma shape k and scale theta (or rate beta); level. DITANYAKAN: Aggregate moments and quantile. RUMUS: Card V6 default (a): scale theta, E[X] = k theta, E[X^2] = k(k+1) theta^2; rate form: theta = 1/beta. scipy gamma(a=k, scale=theta). FFT as Core 5. JAWAB: 1) map parameters per V6. 2) moments. 3) FFT pmf, VaR. 4) check mean.
formulas: E[X] = k theta, E[X^2] = k(k+1) theta^2
pitfalls: scale vs rate confusion changes mean by theta^2

title: Claim count model fit: Poisson vs negative binomial
deliverables: summary json: lambda_poisson, r, beta, dispersion_index, loglik_each
frame: DIKETAHUI: counts per period [n]. DITANYAKAN: Poisson lambda, NB (r, beta) by moments/MLE, dispersion index, preferred model. RUMUS: Poisson MLE lambda = mean; NB MoM: beta = var/mean - 1, r = mean/beta (needs var > mean); dispersion = var(ddof=1)/mean; compare log-likelihoods/AIC. JAWAB: 1) mean, var. 2) fits. 3) LL each. 4) choose by AIC. 5) check dispersion > 1 justifies NB.
pitfalls: var <= mean: NB undefined; keep Poisson

title: Per-claim deductible and limit (layer) on aggregate loss
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda, severity F, deductible d, limit u (per claim). DITANYAKAN: Per-claim payment Y = min(max(X - d, 0), u - d) moments; aggregate moments/quantile. RUMUS: E[Y] = E[X ^ u] - E[X ^ d] (limited expected values); count of nonzero payments thinned: lambda (1 - F(d)) if per-payment; aggregate via FFT on Y pmf. JAWAB: 1) LEVs. 2) per-loss vs per-payment basis. 3) discretise Y. 4) FFT/Panjer. 5) check E[Y] <= u - d.
pitfalls: per-loss vs per-payment frequency mismatch

title: Stop-loss premium from the aggregate pmf
frame: DIKETAHUI: aggregate pmf g [n] on span h (from FFT/Panjer); retentions d [m]. DITANYAKAN: E[(S - d)+] per retention. RUMUS: E[(S-d)+] = E[S] - sum_{x<d} x g(x) - d (1 - F(d-)); or sum_x max(x - d, 0) g(x). JAWAB: 1) grid x = k h. 2) per d sum. 3) check decreasing convex in d, equals E[S] at d = 0.

title: Lattice span and length selection to avoid aliasing
deliverables: summary json: h, n, tail_mass, mass_check
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda, severity distribution, target level. DITANYAKAN: h and n so that the aggregate tail beyond n h is negligible. RUMUS: Card 5 span rule; toolkit suggest_lattice(lam, severity_dist, level, tail_prob); next power of 2; pad with zeros (2x). JAWAB: 1) bound tail via mean + many sd or severity quantile. 2) h = quantile/n. 3) run FFT, check pmf mass near n h ~ 0 and mean error. 4) report h, n.
pitfalls: mass at small x rising when n h too short

title: OU parameters from AR(1) on levels, exact discretisation
deliverables: summary json: a, b, sigma_e, kappa, theta, sigma, half_life
frame: DIKETAHUI: levels x [T+1] (sorted dates), dt (years; daily 1/252). DITANYAKAN: kappa (per year), theta (native units), sigma (per sqrt year), half-life (years and days). RUMUS: Card 6: OLS x_{t+1} = a + b x_t + e; kappa = -ln b/dt, theta = a/(1-b), sigma = sd(e) sqrt(2kappa/(1-b^2)); toolkit ar1_fit(x), ou_from_ar1(a, phi, sigma_e, dt). JAWAB: 1) pairs [T]. 2) ar1_fit. 3) check 0 < b < 1. 4) ou_from_ar1 with dt. 5) half-life ln2/kappa; x252 for trading days. 6) check theta near sample mean.
pitfalls: Euler inversion when exact is implied (V1)

title: OU parameters from AR(1), Euler mapping variant
deliverables: summary json: kappa_euler, theta, sigma_euler, kappa_exact
frame: DIKETAHUI: levels x [T+1], dt; task says Euler / regression of changes. DITANYAKAN: kappa = (1-b)/dt, theta, sigma = sd(e)/sqrt(dt); compare with exact. RUMUS: Card 6 Euler map: dx = alpha + beta x + e -> kappa = -beta/dt, theta = -alpha/beta, sigma = sd(e)/sqrt(dt) (equivalent to b = 1 + beta). JAWAB: 1) regress dx on x (or x_{t+1} on x_t). 2) Euler map. 3) also exact for reference. 4) report the named one.
pitfalls: Euler and exact differ by O(kappa dt)

title: OU half-life in observation periods vs days
frame: DIKETAHUI: series [T+1] with given frequency; dt basis (1/252 or 1/365). DITANYAKAN: Half-life in periods, trading days, years. RUMUS: HL_periods = -ln2/ln b; HL_years = HL_periods dt; ou_from_ar1 with dt=1 gives periods. JAWAB: 1) ar1_fit. 2) HL in periods. 3) convert with dt. 4) check b in (0,1), else NaN with note.
pitfalls: reporting kappa per period as per year

title: OU conditional mean and variance forecast at horizons
deliverables: table: tau, mean, variance, lower, upper
frame: DIKETAHUI: kappa, theta, sigma (per year), x0 (default last observation), horizons tau [n_h], level. DITANYAKAN: E[X_tau], Var[X_tau], two-sided interval per horizon. RUMUS: Card 7: e = e^{-kappa tau}; E = theta + (x0-theta)e; Var = sigma^2 (1-e^2)/(2kappa); interval E +- z sqrt(Var). JAWAB: 1) per horizon e. 2) moments. 3) intervals. 4) check mean -> theta, Var increasing to sigma^2/(2kappa).
formulas: Var = sigma^2(1 - e^{-2 kappa tau})/(2 kappa)

title: OU stationary distribution and band probabilities
deliverables: summary json: stat_mean, stat_sd, prob_in_band, prob_above
frame: DIKETAHUI: kappa, theta, sigma; band [L, U] or level c. DITANYAKAN: Stationary mean/sd and probabilities of being inside/above levels. RUMUS: Card 7 stationary: N(theta, sigma^2/(2kappa)); P = N((U-theta)/sd) - N((L-theta)/sd). JAWAB: 1) sd = sigma/sqrt(2kappa). 2) probabilities. 3) compare with empirical frequency of the data.

title: OU exact simulation and moment check
deliverables: summary json: sim_mean, sim_var, theory_mean, theory_var
frame: DIKETAHUI: kappa, theta, sigma, x0, T, n_steps, n_paths, seed (rng API named). DITANYAKAN: Paths and terminal mean/variance vs theory. RUMUS: Card 6 exact step: x' = theta + (x - theta)e^{-kappa dt} + sigma sqrt((1-e^{-2kappa dt})/(2kappa)) Z. JAWAB: 1) rng per V5. 2) loop steps (include t=0 column). 3) terminal moments (ddof=1). 4) theory Card 7. 5) check within MC error.
formulas: x_{t+dt} = theta + (x_t - theta)e^{-kappa dt} + sigma sqrt((1-e^{-2 kappa dt})/(2 kappa)) Z
pitfalls: legacy np.random.seed vs default_rng give different draws

title: Euler discretisation bias for OU vs exact scheme
frame: DIKETAHUI: kappa, theta, sigma, x0, T; step counts [m]; n_paths, seed. DITANYAKAN: Terminal variance under Euler vs exact by step size; bias. RUMUS: Euler: x' = x + kappa(theta - x)dt + sigma sqrt(dt) Z; its stationary var sigma^2 dt/(1-(1-kappa dt)^2) vs sigma^2/(2kappa). JAWAB: 1) same Z for both schemes. 2) per dt, terminal variance. 3) analytic Euler variance. 4) check bias -> 0 linearly in dt.
formulas: Var_euler,inf = sigma^2 dt/(2 kappa dt - kappa^2 dt^2)

title: OU maximum likelihood via exact Gaussian transition
deliverables: summary json: kappa, theta, sigma, loglik
frame: DIKETAHUI: levels x [T+1], dt. DITANYAKAN: MLE kappa, theta, sigma and log-likelihood. RUMUS: Conditional x_{t+1} | x_t ~ N(theta + (x_t - theta)e^{-kappa dt}, sigma^2(1-e^{-2kappa dt})/(2kappa)); MLE equals OLS AR(1) with variance ddof=0 (sd(e) with n, not n-2). JAWAB: 1) OLS start. 2) maximise LL (or closed form). 3) map to kappa, theta, sigma. 4) LL value. 5) check vs ar1_fit (differs only by ddof).
formulas: LL = -n/2 ln(2 pi v) - sum (x_{t+1} - m_t)^2/(2v)
pitfalls: ddof: MLE uses n; ar1_fit sigma_e uses n-2

title: OU with additive jumps: moments at horizons
frame: DIKETAHUI: kappa, theta, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J, x0, horizons [n_h]. DITANYAKAN: E and Var of X_tau with jumps; stationary mean. RUMUS: Card 8: E = theta + (x0-theta)e + lambda mu_J(1-e)/kappa; Var = (sigma^2 + lambda(mu_J^2+sigma_J^2))(1-e^2)/(2kappa); stationary mean theta + lambda mu_J/kappa. JAWAB: 1) e per tau. 2) moments. 3) stationary values. 4) check Var increasing. 5) use short-horizon additive approx only if told.
pitfalls: short-horizon add-on lambda mu_J tau only when text says 'add'

title: Jumps from AR(1) residuals and OU-jump calibration
deliverables: summary json: kappa, theta, sigma, n_jumps, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J
frame: DIKETAHUI: levels x [T+1], dt; threshold c (default 3). DITANYAKAN: OU params, jump flags, lambda (per year), mu_J, sigma_J; optional sigma from non-jump residuals. RUMUS: Card conventions: flag |e| > c std(e, ddof=1); lambda = n_jumps/(n_resid dt); OU from ar1_fit/ou_from_ar1. JAWAB: 1) AR(1). 2) residuals [T]. 3) flags. 4) jump stats. 5) re-estimate sigma only if stated. 6) check lambda small, kappa > 0.
pitfalls: refitting the AR(1) without jumps unless told

title: Geometric mean-reverting price: lognormal moments of S
frame: DIKETAHUI: ln S OU params kappa, theta_X, sigma; S0; horizons. DITANYAKAN: E[S_tau], Var[S_tau], median. RUMUS: Card 9: m = theta + (ln S0 - theta)e, v = sigma^2(1-e^2)/(2kappa); E[S] = exp(m + v/2), Var = (e^v - 1) exp(2m + v). JAWAB: 1) X0 = ln S0. 2) m, v per tau. 3) lognormal moments. 4) check E[S] > median.
pitfalls: using theta of S instead of theta of ln S

title: Schwartz one-factor commodity futures curve
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, kappa, mu (or theta_X), sigma, lambda_risk (0 if silent), maturities [n]. DITANYAKAN: Futures prices F(0,T) per maturity. RUMUS: Card 9: theta_X = mu - sigma^2/(2kappa); a* = theta_X - lambda_risk/kappa; ln F = e^{-kappa T} ln S0 + (1-e^{-kappa T}) a* + sigma^2 (1-e^{-2kappa T})/(4kappa). JAWAB: 1) a*. 2) ln F per T. 3) exp. 4) check F(0,0) = S0, F -> exp(a* + sigma^2/(4kappa)).
formulas: ln F(T) = e^{-kT} ln S + (1-e^{-kT}) a* + sigma^2(1-e^{-2kT})/(4k)
pitfalls: confusing mu (level of S drift) with theta_X

title: Schwartz model calibration to an observed futures curve
deliverables: summary json: kappa, a_star, sigma, rmse
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, futures prices F_mkt [n] with maturities [n]; optional sigma from spot history. DITANYAKAN: kappa, a*, (sigma) minimising squared log-price errors. RUMUS: Card 9 futures formula; least squares on ln F; sigma fixed from AR(1) of ln S if given. JAWAB: 1) ln F_mkt. 2) objective. 3) bounded optimisation multi-start. 4) residuals, RMSE. 5) check kappa > 0.

title: Mean-reverting spread trading bands from OU
frame: DIKETAHUI: spread series [T+1] (or two prices and hedge ratio), entry/exit z thresholds, dt. DITANYAKAN: OU fit, stationary sd, z-scores, signals. RUMUS: Card 6-7; z_t = (x_t - theta)/(sigma/sqrt(2kappa)); toolkit ar1_fit, ou_from_ar1. JAWAB: 1) spread. 2) OU fit. 3) z. 4) signals: short above +z_in, long below -z_in, exit at |z| < z_out. 5) check half-life plausible vs sample length.
pitfalls: look-ahead: fitting on the full sample then trading in-sample; state it

title: Up-barrier hit probability via running maximum
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, barrier H > S0 (price), mu, sigma (per year), horizons T [n_h]; measure P or Q. DITANYAKAN: P(max_{t<=T} S_t >= H) per horizon. RUMUS: Card 10 with X = ln(S/S0), b = ln(H/S0), log drift nu = mu - sigma^2/2 (Q: r - q - sigma^2/2); P(M_T < b) = N((b-nu T)/s) - e^{2 nu b/sigma^2} N((-b-nu T)/s); toolkit barrier_hit_prob(S0,H,T,mu,sigma,drift_is_log). JAWAB: 1) b, nu. 2) per T: s = sigma sqrt T. 3) hit = 1 - P(M_T < b). 4) check in [0,1], increasing in T.
formulas: P(M_T >= b) = 1 - N((b - nu T)/s) + e^{2 nu b/sigma^2} N((-b - nu T)/s)
pitfalls: using H - S0 instead of ln(H/S0); arithmetic vs log drift (drift_is_log)

title: Down-barrier hit probability via running minimum
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, H < S0, mu, sigma, horizons [n_h]. DITANYAKAN: P(min S_t <= H) per horizon. RUMUS: Card 10: a = ln(H/S0) < 0; P(m_T > a) = N((-a + nu T)/s) - e^{2 nu a/sigma^2} N((a + nu T)/s); hit = 1 - that; toolkit barrier_hit_prob or running_min_cdf(m, T, nu, sigma). JAWAB: 1) a, nu. 2) per horizon. 3) hit. 4) check sign of exponent with a < 0, monotone in T.
formulas: P(m_T > a) = N((-a + nu T)/s) - e^{2 nu a/sigma^2} N((a + nu T)/s)
pitfalls: reporting P(no hit) as the hit probability

title: First passage time CDF and density (inverse Gaussian)
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, H, mu, sigma, time grid [n_t]. DITANYAKAN: P(tau_b <= t) and density f(t) on the grid. RUMUS: Card 11: P(tau_b <= t) = P(M_t >= b); f(t) = |b|/(sigma sqrt(2 pi t^3)) exp(-(b - nu t)^2/(2 sigma^2 t)); IG(mean b/nu, shape b^2/sigma^2); toolkit first_passage_cdf, first_passage_pdf. JAWAB: 1) b, nu. 2) cdf, pdf per t. 3) check cdf non-decreasing, trapezoid int pdf ~ cdf.
formulas: f(t) = b/(sigma sqrt(2 pi t^3)) exp(-(b - nu t)^2/(2 sigma^2 t))

title: Expected first passage time and probability of ever hitting
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, H, mu, sigma. DITANYAKAN: E[tau_b] (years) and P(tau_b < inf). RUMUS: Card 11: E[tau_b] = b/nu if nu b > 0 (drift toward barrier) else infinite; P(ever) = 1 toward, e^{2 nu b/sigma^2} away (exponent negative); toolkit expected_first_passage_time. JAWAB: 1) b, nu, sign. 2) E[tau]. 3) P(ever). 4) check P <= 1.
formulas: P(ever hit) = exp(2 nu b/sigma^2) when nu b < 0
pitfalls: MC E[tau] averages only finite hits unless told

title: Joint distribution of terminal value and running maximum
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu, sigma, T, levels x <= b (log units, or prices to log). DITANYAKAN: P(X_T <= x, M_T <= b). RUMUS: Card 12: N((x - nu T)/s) - e^{2 nu b/sigma^2} N((x - 2b - nu T)/s). JAWAB: 1) log transform. 2) joint. 3) check <= each marginal; at x = b equals P(M_T <= b).
formulas: P(X_T <= x, M_T <= b) = N((x-nu T)/s) - e^{2 nu b/sigma^2} N((x - 2b - nu T)/s)

title: Monte Carlo hit probabilities with discrete monitoring correction
deliverables: table: horizon, mc_prob, se, closed_form, bgk_closed_form
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, H, mu, sigma, horizons [n_h], dt, n_paths, seed. DITANYAKAN: MC hit probability per horizon with SE; closed form; BGK-shifted closed form. RUMUS: toolkit gbm_paths(S0,mu,sigma,T,n_steps,n_paths,seed), mc_hit_probability(paths,H,dt,horizons,S0); BGK: H' = H e^{+-0.5826 sigma sqrt dt} (away from S0). JAWAB: 1) paths [n_paths x n_steps+1] incl t=0. 2) slice to round(T/dt) steps per horizon. 3) running max/min vs H. 4) p_hat, SE = sqrt(p(1-p)/n). 5) closed form with H and H'. 6) check MC below continuous, near BGK.
pitfalls: discrete daily MC underestimates continuous hits

title: Driftless reflection principle check
frame: DIKETAHUI: b > 0, sigma, T; n_paths, n_steps, seed. DITANYAKAN: P(M_T >= b) = 2N(-b/(sigma sqrt T)) and MC estimate. RUMUS: Card 10 mu = 0 case. JAWAB: 1) closed form. 2) simulate ABM. 3) running max incl 0. 4) compare, |z| < 3 after accounting for discrete bias.

title: Hit probability from data: estimate drift and vol then compute
deliverables: summary json: mu_log, sigma, hit_prob per horizon
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices [T+1] daily, barrier H (price), horizons [n_h]; S0 = last price. DITANYAKAN: Annualised log drift and vol; hit probabilities. RUMUS: Card conventions: nu = mean(log ret)/dt, sigma = std(ddof=1)/sqrt(dt); under Q nu = r - q - sigma^2/2. Card 10 with b = ln(H/S0). JAWAB: 1) log returns. 2) nu, sigma. 3) S0 last. 4) per horizon prob. 5) state measure used.
pitfalls: using arithmetic mean return as log drift without -sigma^2/2

title: Double barrier exit probability by Monte Carlo
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, H_up > S0 > H_low, mu, sigma, horizons, dt, n_paths, seed. DITANYAKAN: Probabilities of exiting first through each barrier and of no exit. RUMUS: toolkit gbm_paths, first_hit_times(paths, H, dt, S0) per barrier; compare first hit times. JAWAB: 1) paths. 2) first hit time per barrier (inf if none). 3) classify per horizon. 4) probabilities sum to 1. 5) single-barrier closed forms bound each.

title: Running max/min distribution table and quantiles
frame: DIKETAHUI: nu, sigma, T, level grid. DITANYAKAN: CDF of M_T and m_T and selected quantiles. RUMUS: Card 10; toolkit running_max_cdf(m, T, nu, sigma), running_min_cdf; quantile by root-finding. JAWAB: 1) grid CDFs. 2) quantiles via brentq. 3) MC check with running_extremes(paths). 4) check CDF monotone, M_T >= 0.
formulas: P(M_T <= m) = N((m - nu T)/s) - e^{2 nu m/sigma^2} N((-m - nu T)/s)

title: Euler vs exact GBM discretisation bias in option pricing
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, K, T, r, sigma; step counts; n_paths, seed. DITANYAKAN: Prices from Euler on S, exact log scheme, and BS. RUMUS: Euler S' = S(1 + r dt + sigma sqrt dt Z); exact S' = S exp((r - sigma^2/2)dt + sigma sqrt dt Z); toolkit bs_price. JAWAB: 1) same Z. 2) per step count both schemes. 3) price diffs. 4) check exact unbiased for any dt; Euler bias O(dt).
formulas: S_{t+dt} = S_t exp((r - sigma^2/2)dt + sigma sqrt(dt) Z)

title: Commodity spot OU from log prices with seasonality removed
deliverables: summary json: kappa, theta, sigma, half_life
frame: DIKETAHUI: spot prices [T+1] with dates; dt. DITANYAKAN: Seasonal component, OU on deseasonalised log price. RUMUS: Card 9 (X = ln S OU); seasonal regression on month dummies or sin/cos; AR(1) on residuals (ar1_fit add_const as stated), ou_from_ar1. JAWAB: 1) ln S. 2) seasonal fit. 3) residual series. 4) AR(1) -> OU. 5) check b in (0,1).

title: OU MC barrier hit probability for a mean-reverting series
frame: DIKETAHUI: kappa, theta, sigma, x0, threshold c, horizons, dt, n_paths, seed. DITANYAKAN: P(X reaches c before horizon) by MC. RUMUS: Card 6 exact simulation; running max/min (include t=0); no simple closed form, so MC with SE. JAWAB: 1) simulate. 2) running extreme vs c. 3) per horizon p and SE. 4) check increasing in horizon; discrete bias noted.

title: Merton jump-diffusion barrier hit probability by MC
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, H, mu, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J, horizons, dt, n_paths, seed. DITANYAKAN: Hit probability with jumps vs pure GBM with same total variance. RUMUS: Card 1 dynamics per step; jumps cause overshoot so continuity correction differs; GBM closed form via barrier_hit_prob. JAWAB: 1) simulate log paths with Poisson jumps. 2) running min. 3) probability per horizon, SE. 4) GBM comparison. 5) check jump case higher for down barrier when mu_J < 0.
formulas: dX = (mu - sigma^2/2 - lambda kbar)dt + sigma dW + dJ

title: Compound Poisson process path simulation and count checks
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda (per year), severity distribution, T, n_paths, seed. DITANYAKAN: Simulated arrivals, counts N_T, cumulative losses; checks vs theory. RUMUS: Interarrival Exp(1/lambda); N_T ~ Pois(lambda T); E[S_T] = lambda T E[X], Var = lambda T E[X^2]. JAWAB: 1) simulate arrivals until T. 2) severities. 3) counts and totals. 4) compare moments; dispersion of counts ~ 1.

title: OU moments in native units vs converted decimals
deliverables: summary json: kappa, theta, sigma in both units
frame: DIKETAHUI: rate/yield levels in percent [T+1], dt; instruction to convert or not. DITANYAKAN: OU parameters in native units and after /100 conversion. RUMUS: Card conventions: kappa invariant to scaling; theta and sigma scale by 1/100; log transforms need decimal first. JAWAB: 1) fit in native units. 2) scale theta, sigma. 3) report in units the text asks. 4) check kappa equal in both.
pitfalls: log of percent levels vs decimals changes nothing in kappa but shifts theta

title: Aggregate loss: compound Poisson normal and shifted-gamma approximations
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda, severity moments E[X], E[X^2], E[X^3]; level. DITANYAKAN: Approximate VaR by normal and translated gamma vs FFT. RUMUS: Moments from Card 5; translated gamma: alpha = 4/skew^2, beta = 2/(skew sd), x0 = mean - 2 sd/skew; VaR = x0 + Gamma^{-1}(level; alpha, scale 1/beta). JAWAB: 1) moments. 2) normal quantile. 3) translated gamma. 4) FFT reference. 5) check normal understates tail.

title: Merton jump-diffusion option delta and gamma
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K [M], T, r, q, sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J. DITANYAKAN: Delta and gamma from the series (analytic) and bump check. RUMUS: Card 2: Delta = sum_n w_n e^{-qT} N(d1_n), Gamma = sum_n w_n e^{-qT} phi(d1_n)/(S sigma_n sqrt T) with r_n, sigma_n; toolkit bs_greeks per term. JAWAB: 1) per term greeks. 2) weighted sums. 3) central bump check. 4) check 0 <= delta <= 1 for calls.
